issues.feedback: The spec keeps `timeout_seconds` as an active runtime fallback and adds `[backends.<name>.role_timeouts]`, which is still backend-scoped. That conflicts with the stated requirement to remove backend-specific timeout configuration and make timeout config per-role (not per-backend).
`prompt_reviewer` is an executing role in orchestration but is not included in the proposed `RoleTimeouts` set. Its timeout would remain non-configurable under this spec.

The plan assumes `acceptance_qa` and `reformatter` timeouts can be applied, but current execution paths pass role `qa` for acceptance QA and pass the original role for reformatter retries. Without explicit call-site/context changes, those role-specific overrides will never be enforced.

PRD/quick-PRD and daemon refinement execute backends outside the orchestrator role flow. The spec does not define how role-based timeout resolution applies there if backend timeout config is removed/refactored.

Schema changes are not enough: `config set/get/show` currently expose `backends.*.timeout_seconds` only. The spec needs explicit behavior for new role-timeout keys and legacy key handling (deprecate, migrate, or reject) to satisfy backward compatibility/migration requirements.

The technical approach is internally inconsistent (Options A/B/C are all marked as chosen, and `claude.rs`/`codex.rs` are described as both requiring and not requiring change). This ambiguity makes implementation riskier than necessary.

Proposed tests miss key edge cases: prompt reviewer timeout, reformatter timeout role selection, acceptance QA role selection, tmux/non-tmux parity for role-based timeouts, and conformance coverage for config migration/CLI behavior.
